title: Rast sweeps the Nürburgring weekend with Race 2 win
dek: René Rast won again from pole, by 2.739 seconds from Paul di Resta, completing a perfect weekend for Audi as a slow pit stop dropped Gary Paffett to fifth.

chapters.title: A new points leader after Saturday
text: Saturday had belonged to Audi and to René Rast, who won Race 1 from pole by 0.862 seconds after Bruno Spengler's BMW closed in over the last laps. The other big story was behind the podium: Paul di Resta was spun by Philipp Eng's BMW, finished last without points and handed the championship lead to his Mercedes-AMG team-mate Gary Paffett, 194 points to 186.

Sunday brought a chance for both to answer. The minimum tyre pressures introduced for the weekend were still in force, the weather stayed dry, and Rast, who had already won the first race, was one qualifying lap away from a second pole.

chapters.title: Rast pole again, by six thousandths
text: Qualifying was again dry and sunny, and again it ended with Rast on top. His 1m22.140s was just 0.006 seconds quicker than Paffett's 1m22.146s, with Eng third on 1m22.159s and Timo Glock fourth on 1m22.203s, so that the first four were covered by only 0.063 seconds. Rast said that when you are on a run you are on a run, after a long dry spell at the start of the year, and Audi's Dieter Gass admitted he had not expected the pole to be repeated.

Lucas Auer and Pascal Wehrlein were fifth and sixth on identical times of 1m22.331s. Mike Rockenfeller was seventh, the next Audi, ahead of Spengler, Marco Wittmann and Joel Eriksson. Di Resta could only qualify 11th on 1m22.566s, with Nico Müller 12th and Augusto Farfus 13th. Daniel Juncadella was 14th and Jamie Green 15th, while Loïc Duval, Robin Frijns and Edoardo Mortara filled the last three places, Mortara 18th on 1m22.925s.

chapters.title: Auer jumps to second, Glock hits him
text: Rast kept the lead at the start, while Auer made the best getaway of all, going from fifth to second and trying a move around the outside that Rast closed by cutting across his exit. Paffett and Eng both lost places in the opening moments. Green's race changed at the end of the first lap when contact left him with tyre damage and he went in for the mandatory stop immediately.

On lap two Glock dived down the inside of the Mercedes at the first corner, hit the side of Auer's car and spun him. The stewards gave Glock a drive-through penalty, he finished 16th, and Auer dropped down the order. With Auer gone, Paffett took over as Rast's closest challenger and used DRS to close in, but Rast defended and eased clear.

chapters.title: Paffett's slow stop opens the door
text: The stops decided the places behind the leader. Rast came in early, and Paffett's stop went wrong: a problem with the right-rear wheel cost him around five seconds and dropped him behind di Resta and the BMWs of Wittmann, Eriksson and Eng. His deficit to Rast grew to about twelve seconds, having been a podium certainty only moments earlier.

Spengler stopped a lap after di Resta, and on cold tyres he could not hold off the Mercedes, which took second place. Di Resta then fought off Wittmann for the position, and Paffett began a recovery, passing Eng and Eriksson within a handful of laps.

chapters.title: Di Resta closes to 2.739 seconds
text: Rast's tyres wore away over the closing stage, as they had on Saturday, and a gap of around ten seconds to di Resta shrank to 2.739 seconds by the flag after 40 laps in 57m17.440s. He said the last part of the race was a fight for survival. Wittmann took third, 3.439 seconds back, with Spengler fourth, Paffett fifth, 7.177 seconds behind, and Eriksson sixth.

Farfus was seventh, Eng started third but finished eighth, and Wehrlein was ninth. Frijns climbed from 17th to tenth and Mortara from 18th to 11th. Müller dropped from the edge of the top ten to 14th, and Green was 15th. Glock was 16th, Juncadella was out after 38 laps, and Auer's race ended after 33. Paffett set the fastest lap, a 1m23.875s on lap 23.

chapters.title: Rast makes history, Paffett's lead cut to two points
text: Rast became the first driver in DTM history to take both poles and both wins in a weekend, the full 56 points on offer. He said it was hard to believe, a weekend that nobody had managed before in the series, and that leading looked easy from the outside but was mentally tough when his tyres were gone and a rival was closing. Gass said he was speechless and had not expected it, given where Audi had started the season, and that Rast's qualifying had been the foundation for both wins. Rast added that the sweep felt similar to winning a championship. Gass later argued that Audi's decision not to ask for rule concessions had been justified, because the car could now win on its own merits after a difficult start to the year.

The weekend also changed the shape of the championship. Paffett kept the lead on 206 points but di Resta, who limited the damage with second place, was only two behind on 204. Rast climbed to third on 149, the best non-Mercedes driver and 57 points off the lead, with Mortara fourth on 138 and Wittmann fifth on 137.

Paffett congratulated Rast and was blunt about his own result. He said the slow stop was frustrating because he had been comfortably second and then had to fight for fifth, costing the team a lot of points. BMW's Jens Marquardt called Rast's form fantastic. Mercedes team principal Ulrich Fritz, who called it stellar, said the pace had been better than on Saturday, that Paffett had driven well to limit the damage and that di Resta's second place was worth a lot, and the team would analyse both races to find answers before the next round.

That round is at the Red Bull Ring in Spielberg, two weeks later on 21 to 23 September, followed by the finale at Hockenheim on 13 and 14 October. Only two rounds remained, and Rast, 57 points back, would need a great deal to go his way.

facts.v: René Rast took both poles and both race wins at the Nürburgring, the first driver in DTM history to do so, and collected the maximum 56 points.
